purpose: Machine-readable replay inputs for the F1 transfer-benchmark falsifier's Arm C. The per-seed numbers existed ONLY inside a markdown table, so Arm C would otherwise have had to hard-code twelve literals -- an assertion that can silently drift from its source. These values are HAND-TRANSCRIBED and then VERIFIED against the markdown by tests/test_g2_replay_fixture.py, which re-parses the table. Verified, never trusted.

global_r2.note: the ONLY metric the embedding wins, and the one most polluted by population structure. Arm C turns on this: the verdict must still come out NEGATIVE despite a win here.

within_group_r2.note: the de-confounded metric. Negative across all three seeds -- the signature of the recorded failure: the embedding learned population structure, not the flowering-time signal.

parsing_notes: The markdown minus signs are U+2212 MINUS SIGN (bytes E2 88 92), NOT ASCII hyphen-minus. float('−0.173') raises ValueError; any parser must normalise first.
Row labels carry r² as U+00B2 SUPERSCRIPT TWO, and the within-group row is wrapped in markdown bold with a ' (de-confounded)' suffix.
The structure-only within-group cell is written '+0.038' with an explicit leading plus.
